$comment: Per-service memory ceilings for KDE Plasma 6 desktop services.
Why this module exists: 2026-04-28 21:15 KWin OOM-style death from a
used 692M + 983M swap, ksystemstats had a runaway leak (42min CPU,
known KDE 6.2.x bug). When KWin's INTERNAL allocation fails, the whole
Wayland session dies and SDDM kicks back to login. earlyoom would NOT
have helped — it has --avoid for these very services (correct: you
don't want earlyoom killing kwin under any circumstance).
1. systemd user drop-ins with MemoryHigh/MemoryMax per leaky service
2. Periodic watchdog timer that proactively restarts before the cap
MemoryHigh       = soft throttle (process paused for memory reclaim)
MemoryMax        = hard ceiling (systemd kills the unit; Plasma respawns)
watchdog_warn_mb = proactive threshold (restart BEFORE the ceiling)
Sized for Surface Pro 8 (8GB RAM, 8 logical CPUs).
Adding services is data-driven: edit this JSON, no script change needed.

plasma-kwin_wayland.service._note: Restarting kwin tears the Wayland session — only notify, NEVER auto-restart. Hard ceiling 2.5G lets systemd kill kwin if it truly runs away; Plasma can respawn it.

plasma-plasmashell.service._note: 2026-07-31: 1000M/1800M was too tight — normal working set (~1.03G+) sat above MemoryHigh, causing sustained memory.high direct-reclaim throttle (memory.events high=259229) that froze/crashed the shell twice with no OOM and low aggregate PSI (Never-Freeze v3 mechanism, matches the 2026-07-10 13:06 user-1000.slice incident at service-unit scope). Widened so normal usage stays under MemoryHigh; MemoryMax kept well below the 8GB host ceiling. Plasmashell restart is in-place safe; user sees panel flicker only.

plasma-ksystemstats.service._note: Known leak in KDE 6.2.x — recycle aggressively, no UI impact.

plasma-kded6.service._note: Defense in depth — kded daemons can leak; restart is invisible.
